extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants / patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance from the MPEP on when and how affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be used to antedate references to overcome 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections, including who may sign, evidentiary requirements (conception, reduction to practice, diligence), genus/species rules, exhibit and timing requirements, and examiner review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must show possession of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference being antedated
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection by showing completion of the invention by applicant prior to the effective date of any of the references; the 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit must show possession of either the whole invention as claimed or something falling within the claim(s) prior to the effective date of the reference being antedated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not enough merely to show possession of what the reference happens to show if the reference does not teach the basic inventive concept. Even if the affidavit is not fully commensurate with the rejected claim, the affidavit must still establish possession of the claimed invention, not just what the reference shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind one of a plurality of combined references
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may antedate one reference in a combination of references and need not antedate the reference with the earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a claim has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on Reference A in view of Reference B (with B earlier), the applicant can rely on teachings of Reference B to show that differences between the applicant's affidavit/declaration and the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill prior to the date of Reference A. However, the affidavit/declaration must still establish possession of the claimed invention as to the reference being antedated.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule for antedating generic claims by a single species
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference or activity applied against generic claims may (in most cases) be antedated as to such claims by an affidavit or declaration showing completion of the invention of only a single species within the genus prior to the effective date of the reference or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies assuming the reference/activity is not a statutory bar or a patent/application publication claiming the same invention. See exceptions for unpredictable arts (MPEP § 715.03). Authorities cited: Ex parte Biesecker; In re Fong; In re Defano.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species rules when predictability is in question
rubrics_metrics.description: Where generic claims have been rejected on a reference which discloses a species not antedated by the affidavit, the affidavit will not ordinarily be withdrawn unless applicant can establish possession of the generic invention prior to the reference date (i.e., affidavit must show as much as the minimum disclosure required by a patent specification to support a generic claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reference discloses a claimed species, overcome by showing prior completion of that species or a different species plus a showing the claimed species would have been an obvious modification. If the reference discloses several species of a genus, applicant must show prior completion of all species shown to overcome directly. Alternatively, applicant may show prior completion of one or more species sufficient to infer generic applicability — the test is whether the species completed provide an adequate basis for inferring generic applicability (examples: small genera like halogens vs large genera). Case law cited: In re Spiller; In re Stempel; In re Clarke; In re Plumb; In re Hostettler; In re Mantell; In re Rainer; In re Shokal; In re Schaub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species versus embodiments distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: References which disclose one or more embodiments of a single claimed invention (as opposed to species of a claimed genus) can be overcome by filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing prior completion of a single embodiment of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: where invention is viewed as the use of a component (e.g., PVP as a soil-suspending agent) irrespective of particular detergents, references showing different embodiments are treated as embodiments of a single invention rather than species of a genus. See In re Fong and In re Defano.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations to overcome a rejection must be made by the inventor(s) of the subject matter of the rejected claim(s), a party qualified under 37 CFR 1.42/1.43/1.47 where inventors are unavailable, or the assignee/other party in interest when inventor affidavit is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All inventors of the subject matter may sign. An affidavit by fewer than all named inventors is accepted where it is shown those signers invented the subject matter of the rejected claims (e.g., one of two joint inventors is sole inventor of the claim). Where some named inventors are deceased, refuse to sign, or unavailable, signatures of remaining inventors suffice but the affidavit must show completion by all joint inventors of the subject matter of the rejected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit is a statement in writing made under oath before an authorized officer; a declaration (per 37 CFR 1.68) may be used instead of an affidavit but must include specific statutory acknowledgments and statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaration must include an acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and may jeopardize validity of the application; the declarant must state which statements are of personal knowledge and which are on information and belief. See MPEP § 604–604.06 for more on formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 ineffective against certain U.S. patents or publications claiming the same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is ineffective to overcome a U.S. patent or patent application publication claiming the same invention when the publication date is less than one year prior to presentation of claims — applicant's remedy must be by 37 CFR 1.608; where publication date is 1 year or more prior, rejection under 35 U.S.C. 135(b) should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where domestic reference and application/patent under reexamination are commonly owned and claims are not identical but not patentably distinct, a terminal disclaimer and an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 may be used to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection (see MPEP §718). If claims are identical or not patentably distinct, the items claim the 'same patentable invention' (see 37 CFR 1.601(n)) and 1.131 cannot be used to avoid an interference; allowing 1.131 here would permit issuing two patents to the same invention. Form paragraphs (e.g., 23.14, 23.14.01) may be used for rejections under 135(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and test for 'same patentable invention'
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention 'A' is the same patentable invention as invention 'B' when A is the same as (35 U.S.C. 102) or is obvious (35 U.S.C. 103) in view of B assuming B is prior art with respect to A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because 37 CFR 1.131 defines 'same patentable invention' similarly to interference rules (37 CFR 1.601(n)), an applicant cannot both avoid an interference by using 1.131 and be denied an interference on the grounds claims are not substantially the same. See case law (In re Eickmeyer) for nuances where an applicant may nonetheless file a 1.131 affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts and documentary evidence required (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential thing to be shown under 37 CFR 1.131 is priority of invention demonstrated by FACTS, not conclusions; exhibits may accompany the affidavit/declaration and each exhibit relied upon should be specifically referred to in terms of what it shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable supporting evidence: attached sketches, blueprints, photographs, reproductions of notebook entries, an accompanying model, supporting witness statements, testimony from an interference, and disclosure documents (MPEP §1706). A general allegation of completion prior to the reference is insufficient; declarations asserting conclusion without supporting facts are insufficient. Exhibits and models must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain exhibits and identify exact facts relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration and exhibits must clearly explain which facts or data the applicant is relying on to show completion of the invention prior to the particular date; vague and general statements are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must give a clear explanation of the exhibits pointing out exactly what facts are established and relied upon. Vague descriptions plus general assertions amount to mere pleading and will not satisfy 37 CFR 1.131(b). If interference testimony is used, applicant must point out the parts of the testimony relied on; examiners will not search entire records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals/photocopies of exhibits and handling of missing originals
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131(b) requires that original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, accompany and form part of the affidavit/declaration or their absence be satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sketches/models were made but lost, reproduce and furnish them; if verbal disclosures are relied on, the witness should state as nearly as possible the language used. If dates on exhibits were removed or blocked, dates can be established in the body of the oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of dates and use of approximate dates
rubrics_metrics.description: When alleging conception or reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, the dates in the oath/declaration may be actual dates or may allege that acts occurred prior to a specified date if the applicant does not wish to disclose actual dates. However, actual dates of acts relied on to establish diligence must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence requires actual dates to evaluate continuity of activity; mere allegation that acts occurred prior to a date without factual support is insufficient for diligence evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ways to show prior invention under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must state facts and produce documentary evidence sufficient to show one of: (A) reduction to practice prior to the effective date; (B) conception prior to the effective date plus due diligence from prior to the reference date to a subsequent actual reduction to practice; or (C) conception prior to the effective date plus due diligence from prior to the reference date to the filing date of the application (constructive reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception alone is not a complete invention unless followed by reasonable diligence culminating in reduction to practice or filing. Proof of actual reduction to practice generally requires showing the apparatus actually existed and worked for its intended purpose, but for simple devices mere construction may suffice. Where proof of utility is required depends on whether the reference discloses a utility; the ultimate issue is satisfaction to a reasonable certainty that the subject matter possessed the alleged utility. Unlike interference practice, averments in a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration do not require corroboration; applicant may rely on his/her own affidavit/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence requirement specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When conception occurs prior to the reference but reduction to practice occurs after, applicant must show facts establishing diligence from just prior to the reference date until reduction to practice (actual or constructive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence need not be considered unless conception prior to the effective date is clearly established. In patent law an inventor is either diligent at a given time or not — degrees don't apply; inactivity must be excused and the record must set forth explanation. The critical period begins just prior to the effective date of the reference and ends with the date of reduction to practice (actual or filing). The lapse of time between completion/reduction to practice and filing is not relevant to a 1.131 affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference testimony sometimes usable in lieu of a 1.131 affidavit
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony given by the applicant in an interference may sometimes be used to antedate a reference instead of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must point out the part(s) of the testimony that form the basis of priority over the reference; examiners cannot be expected to search entire interference records for the relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts relied upon must have been carried out in the U.S. or NAFTA/WTO member country
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 104 limits establishment of a date of invention in PTO proceedings to acts carried out in the United States, a NAFTA country, or a WTO member country (subject to effective-date limitations). The 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must allege that the acts relied upon occurred in such a country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can establish a date of completion in a NAFTA member country on or after Dec 8, 1993 and in a WTO member country (other than NAFTA) on or after Jan 1, 1996. Acts occurring prior to those effective dates may be relied upon to show completion, but a date of completion may not be established under 1.131 before those effective dates in those countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and compliance requirements for exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits filed as part of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into an application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits that do not comply with 37 CFR 1.91 may be disposed of or returned to applicant at the Office's discretion. See MPEP §608.03(a) for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who reviews sufficiency and procedures for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of sufficiency of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 should be reviewed and decided by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of formal sufficiency and propriety are by petition answered by Technology Center Directors (MPEP §1002.02(c)). Review on the merits of a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration is by appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonable presentation (timeliness) of affidavits/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 must be timely presented to be admitted; they are considered timely if submitted prior to a final rejection, before appeal in an application not having a final rejection, or after final rejection under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After final rejection, timely submissions include: (1) with a first reply after final to overcome a new ground/requirement in the final rejection; (2) with a satisfactory showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) or 1.195; or (3) under 37 CFR 1.129(a). All admitted affidavits/declarations are acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next succeeding action. For affidavits/declarations filed after appeal, see 37 CFR 1.195 and MPEP §1211.02.
